9.name: Release combination
9.note: Full mapping extracted 2026-08-21 via pdfplumber word-coordinate extraction of catalog page 25 'Release combination' table, then cross-checked and corrected against a clean reference image of the same table provided by the user (removed one erroneous row - a phantom 3rd U-family combination - that the coordinate extraction had introduced). Legend: shunt release 30 ms; shunt release 45 ms; undervoltage release; C.t.-operated release; C.t.-operated release with tripping pulse >=0.1 Ws (20 Ohm). Footnotes: 1) operating voltage for the 1st/2nd release is selected at positions 11-12 (table-wide, not row-specific); 2) a 3rd release is only available for circuit-breakers with a wide housing (table-wide note, applies to any row using a 3rd release - i.e. the S/T/U/V families - not a specific single row); 3) operating voltage for the shunt release is selected with order code Jxx, see page 31 (attached to the two rows where a shunt release appears as the 3rd release: B/F15 and S). 'Other release combinations on request' per catalog.

codes.B: 1st release: shunt release 30 ms, plus a 2nd and/or 3rd release using shunt-release entries - see release_combination_table for the exact row (order code G39 when 2nd release = shunt 30 ms; no order code when 2nd release = shunt 45 ms; order code F15 when 2nd = shunt 45 ms and 3rd = shunt 45 ms, footnote 3 applies)

codes.S: 1st release: shunt release 30 ms; 2nd release: undervoltage release; 3rd release: shunt release 45 ms (footnote 3: shunt voltage selected via order code Jxx)

11.note: Verified 2026-08-21 against catalog page 27 'Operating voltage of the 1st release' table. Position 11 has NO '0' option (a 1st/shunt release always exists per position 9) - standard codes run 1-8, special voltages use digit 9 plus an L1x order code.

12.name: Operating voltage of the 2nd release
12.note: Added 2026-08-21, verified against catalog page 27 'Operating voltage of the 2nd release' table (previously NOT independently decoded - decoder.py incorrectly reused position 11's value/meaning for both positions). position_5_special_series.trigger: Position 5 digit not in the standard table {0,1,2,3,4}

confirmed_values.5: 12 kV special/extended sub-series (article numbers like 3AE55xx-x, e.g. 3AE5554, 3AE5555, 3AE5564, 3AE5565, 3AE5566) - covers higher-current variants (up to 2500A) not represented in the standard 0-4 digit voltage-tier table.
confirmed_values.6: 17.5 kV special/extended sub-series (article numbers like 3AE562x-x, 3AE565x-x, 3AE566x-x, e.g. 3AE5624, 3AE5654, 3AE5655, 3AE5656, 3AE5664, 3AE5665, 3AE5666) - covers higher-current variants (up to 4000A) not represented in the standard 0-4 digit voltage-tier table. Pattern: standard tier digit (2) + 4 = 6.
confirmed_values.7: 24 kV special/extended sub-series (article numbers like 3AE571x-x, 3AE574x-x, e.g. 3AE5714, 3AE5744) - covers higher-current variants (up to 2000A) not represented in the standard 0-4 digit voltage-tier table. Pattern: standard tier digit (3) + 4 = 7.

position_5_special_series.rule: Do NOT treat as an error. Resolve the true voltage tier via primary_article_technical_data_full.csv (tier_kv column) instead of the position-5 digit table. GENERAL PATTERN CONFIRMED 2026-08-20: the special/extended series digit = standard tier digit + 4 (12kV: 1+4=5, 17.5kV: 2+4=6, 24kV: 3+4=7). 7.2kV (0) and 36kV (4) show no such special series in the current data (0 rows found for digit 4 or any offset digit under those tiers).
position_5_special_series.verified: 2026-08-20: Confirmed via primary_article_technical_data_full.csv (359 rows) by grouping all articles per tier by their position-5 digit. Results: digit '5' -> 24 rows, all tier_kv=12 (100%). Digit '6' -> 25 rows, all tier_kv=17.5 (100%). Digit '7' -> 5 rows, all tier_kv=24 (100%). No mixed or ambiguous cases found. Extends the original 12kV-only exception to a general +4-offset rule.

w88_w89_per_article_position13.description: W88/W89 position-13 requirements are set PER EXACT ARTICLE, not just per voltage tier, and further split by manual vs motorized racking variant. Source: user-corrected article_option_compatibility.csv columns W88_manual_pos13 / W88_motorized_pos13 / W89_manual_pos13 / W89_motorized_pos13, installed 2026-08-21 after the user's manual catalog review superseded the earlier tier-only table (see w88_w89_tier_dependent_position13.description for why).
w88_w89_per_article_position13.enforcement: decoder.py looks up the exact base article number (first 8 positions) in article_option_compatibility.csv. Manual vs motorized variant is selected by whether M04 or M05 (motorized third-party racking order codes) is present in the input's order codes - if so, the *_motorized_pos13 column is used, otherwise *_manual_pos13. A blank column value means that code is not offered at all for that exact article/variant (INVALID if used); a non-blank value lists the allowed position-13 value(s) (INVALID if position 13 doesn't match one of them); if the article itself isn't found in the CSV, the check reports UNRESOLVED rather than guessing.
w88_w89_per_article_position13.verified: 2026-08-21: corrected data confirms W88 IS offered at 24kV for at least 16 articles (e.g. 3AE5322-1, W88_manual_pos13=1), reversing the prior tier-level NOT OFFERED claim. All 81 rows the user corrected strictly widened the previously-known allowed set (no narrowing, no out-of-range values vs. the documented position-13 code set {0,1,2,3,5,6}). Regression-tested against 7.2/12/17.5/24kV rows with both old (narrower) and newly-widened values, plus manual/motorized M04/M05 selection.

d59_standard_semantics.description: The article-level compatibility table has two mutually-exclusive markers per article: 'D59 standard compulsory' and 'D59 optional'. Confirmed by user 2026-08-20. CSV columns renamed 2026-08-21 (from standard_available/D59_available) so D59 is the primary concept, split into these two named states.

rule.D59_standard_compulsory=YES: Standard housing is COMPULSORY for this exact article/rating - D59 (wide housing) is NOT offered as an alternative. No customer choice here.
rule.D59_optional=YES: D59 (wide housing) is a valid OPTIONAL order code for this exact article - the customer decides whether to add it or not. If not added, the base article still ships correctly (standard is not implied to be forbidden by D59 being available; D59 is an addable extra).
rule.both=NO (20 of 360 rows): Neither flag is documented YES for this article in the compatibility table. Treated by decoder.py as UNRESOLVED, not silently valid or invalid - needs manual catalog review, not yet root-caused as of 2026-08-21.

d59_standard_semantics.enforcement: decoder.py's find_option_compatibility() looks up the exact base article number (first 8 positions) in article_option_compatibility.csv. If the input includes the D59 order code: D59_optional=YES passes; D59_standard_compulsory=YES (and D59_optional!=YES) is flagged INVALID; both=NO is flagged UNRESOLVED.
d59_standard_semantics.verified: 2026-08-20: tested against 3AE5002-1/3AE5012-1/3AE5322-1 (D59_optional=YES, should pass) and 3AE5322-4 (D59_standard_compulsory=YES, D59_optional=NO, should flag if D59 is used). 2026-08-21: CSV columns renamed from standard_available/D59_available to D59_standard_compulsory/D59_optional; decoder.py and this entry updated to match; 0 mapping mismatches vs. pre-rename backup across all 360 rows.
